name: Green hydrogen in refineries
principle: A PEM electrolyser on renewable electricity supplies hydrogen to refinery hydroprocessing in place of some steam-reformer hydrogen. Shell's REFHYNE at its Rheinland site is a 10 MW PEM unit built by ITM Power, producing up to 1,300 t/yr, with expansion to 100 MW planned.

suppliers.name: ITM Power
suppliers.product: 10 MW PEM electrolyser for Shell Rheinland

performance.basis: 10 MW PEM; plans for 100 MW at Rheinland

source.note: Hydrocarbon Engineering, Shell starts up PEM green hydrogen electrolyser in Europe, 5 July 2021

reference_plants.name: REFHYNE, Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Rheinland
reference_plants.capacity: 10 MW PEM, up to 1,300 t/yr H2

costs.basis: annex table column 2024 (dollar year not explicitly stated); same system boundary as the global-average entry; STEPS 2030 projection: 450-900 USD/kWe

costs.metric: electrolyser CAPEX for European projects by equipment origin
costs.basis: USD 2300/kW with all-European equipment, 2150 with Chinese stack only, 1800 with Chinese stack and BoP; electrolyser efficiency 62% (European) versus 56% (Chinese components); EPC and contingency at European prices

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025, Figure 3.16 notes (page 112)

costs.metric: merchant renewable hydrogen tender price for refinery supply (India, awarded bids)
costs.basis: build-own-operate tenders, status August 2025, dollar year not stated: Indian Oil Panipat 10 kt awarded to L&T Energy Green Tech at INR 397/kg H2 (~USD 4.6/kg), project at FID; BPCL Bina and HPCL Visakh 5 kt each awarded to Ocior Energy at INR 328/kg H2 (~USD 3.8/kg)

costs.metric: levelised cost of hydrogen, renewable electrolytic, STEPS 2030 projection
costs.basis: Stated Policies Scenario 2030, in USD (2024): regions in China, the Middle East, Australia and some areas of the United States can reduce renewable hydrogen production cost to USD 2-4/kg (China's lower end close to under USD 2/kg)

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025, Chapter 3 text on Figures 3.8 and 3.9 (pages 94 and 97)

advantages: Replaces fossil hydrogen at point of use
limitations: Scale: 10 MW is small against refinery hydrogen demand (not quantified by the source)
